liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the Other One excellent, recalling a Cornell girl on their shoulders through the second set; Space is included within The Other One on this transfer [1][22]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer thinks the Dew opened the second set to calm the crowd, then went into Playin' [26]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Opener suited the rough crowd; Jerry's odd segue notes in the chorus, solid fast-paced version [28]
- **Loser** (1 review): Good version, and the crowd was surprisingly enthusiastic for it [28]
- **Take A Step Back/Addam's Family Tuning** (1 review): Funk-flavored Step Back game was fun, per reviewer [28]
- **The Wicked Messenger** (1 review): Reviewer knows a bootleg of Dead playing Dylan songs with this from soundboard [30]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd87-07-12 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t03 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t04 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t05 Loser**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t06 Tons Of Steel**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t07 Take A Step Back**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t08 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd87-07-12 t09 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-07-12.142137.fob.schoeps.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 36 songs; 216 min [1]
- **gd1987-07-12.137179.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 219 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1987-07-12.137181.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 219 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1987-07-12.sbd-aud.miller.84266.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 214 min; rated 3/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd87-07-12.sbd.agan.3860.sbefail.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 205 min; rated 3.38/5 by 21 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording quality pretty good; Reviewer believes the Dylan set is probably soundboard, and says an audience recording is better than the soundboard; Reviewer recalls the sound being phenomenal compared to other stadium shows [23][24][25]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: gd87-07-12 t01 Crowd [1]
- Hot New Jersey summer night; the band jammed, and Dylan was good though reviewer has heard better [23]
- Reviewer queued in Jersey for tickets about a month ahead; this was their only Dead show [25]
- Rowdy vibe after a long hot day in the lot; fans jumped onto a increasingly packed floor [26]
- Giants Stadium felt too big; reviewer sat far back among rude, smelly New Yorkers [27]
- Crowd was amped up, with many new Touch of Grey fans; reviewer tripped running in from the gate [33]
- Third set featured Bob Dylan on acoustic guitar, with Jerry Garcia on guitar and pedal steel [1]
- Third set had Bob Dylan on acoustic guitar; Garcia played guitar and pedal steel [2]
- Reviewer says this show had two sets before Dylan, unlike the JFK show [26]
- Reviewer ranks the Dead/Dylan portion above Foxboro but below JFK [27]
- Reviewer's first show was JFK on the 10th, less intimidating because it was their hometown [29]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-07-12.142137.fob.schoeps.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: 1st & 2nd Set: (FOB) Schoeps > PCM > PCM; 3rd Set: (FOB) Schoeps > PCM > Dat > CD (shnid 84266); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD… [1]
- **gd1987-07-12.137179.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shnid=84266) Recording Info: Sets 1 & 2: SBD -> PCM -> Dat -> CD Set 3: (FOB) Schoeps -> PCM -> Dat -> CD Transfer Info: CD ->… [2]. Also: Matrix mix of three sources, soundboard plus audience, made by an archive.org user and converted to FLAC in 2016 [2]
- **gd1987-07-12.137181.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: flac16/48kHz ; 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) - SBD (shnid=84266) SRecording Info: Sets 1 & 2: SBD -> PCM -> Dat -> CD Set 3: (FOB) Schoeps -> PCM -> Dat -> CD… [3]. Also: 5.1 surround mix in Adobe Audition CC 2014 by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in 2016 [3]
- **gd1987-07-12.sbd-aud.miller.84266.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sets 1 & 2: SBD -> PCM -> Dat -> CD ; Set 3: (FOB) Schoeps -> PCM -> Dat -> CD [4]. Also: Miller did DAT to CD transfers in 2000; the soundboard is an UltraMatrix containing much audience [4]
- **gd87-07-12.sbd.agan.3860.sbefail.shnf**: source: AUD FOB CM> C> Nak DR-10 (Playback)> Midiman Flying Cow 24bit/48kHz [10]. Also: Reviewer asks whether anyone has the original soundboard of the third set [24]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.rarenewspapers.com: [1987 "Bob Dylan & Grateful Dead" at Giants Stadium... | RareNewspapers.com](https://www.rarenewspapers.com/view/718795) [36]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - Giants Stadium 1987-07-12 | Caine Schneider | Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/48766396968/) [37]
